verses.english: The Venerable Rādha went up to the Buddha …

verses.pali: ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
“sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṅkhittena dhammaṁ desetu, yamahaṁ bhagavato dhammaṁ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyyan”ti.
verses.english: “Sir, may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief. When I’ve heard it, I’ll live alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute.”

verses.pali: “Yaṁ kho, rādha, aniccaṁ tatra te chando pahātabbo.
verses.english: “Rādha, you should give up desire for what is impermanent.

verses.pali: Kiñca, rādha, aniccaṁ tatra te chando pahātabbo?
yampidaṁ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi aniccaṁ. Tatra te chando pahātabbo …pe…
verses.english: And the pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact is also impermanent. You should give up desire for it.

verses.pali: mano anicco. Tatra te chando pahātabbo.
yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi aniccaṁ. Tatra te chando pahātabbo.
verses.english: And the pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact is also impermanent. You should give up desire for it.

verses.pali: Yaṁ kho, rādha, aniccaṁ tatra te chando pahātabbo”ti.
verses.english: You should give up desire for what is impermanent.”
